title: Analysing Impact of Regional Weather on PLC-based Data Transmission in Malaysia, and Nigeria.
summary: A regression-based neural network from Universiti Putra Malaysia predicts how regional weather affects power-line data throughput in Malaysia and Nigeria; no source reports use by a utility.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: The project models relationships between weather and power-line data transmission. On 25 April 2025, the project team at Universiti Putra Malaysia published its results in Transactions on Engineering and Computing Sciences. The authors report that their model predicts a regional throughput performance of 71.62% for Peninsular Malaysia and between 74.46% and 99.97% across six Nigerian regions, from historical weather data supplied by Universiti Putra Malaysia and the Nigerian Meteorological Agency. In June 2025, the project had collected data and developed models for Malaysia and Nigeria, and it remained in research and prototyping. No source attributes a network improvement to the AI, as distinct from infrastructure replacement. No source reports that a utility used these predictions.
purpose: Explain weather-related transmission problems and guide network planning.
system: Analysing Impact of Regional Weather on PLC-based Data Transmission in Malaysia, and Nigeria.
